i18n.A1 — Le processeur de votre ordinat: A1 — The processor of your computer
a1.comp: This is your computer's brain. It thinks and does the calculations. The faster it is, the faster your programs run.
a1.gamme.entree_de_gamme.texte: an i3 is enough for internet, office work and videos, but may struggle if you do heavy tasks
a1.gamme.milieu_de_gamme.texte: an i5 is the most common choice because it offers the best balance between speed and price
a1.gamme.haut_de_gamme.texte: an i7 is fast and comfortable for video editing, creative work and demanding games
a1.gamme.tres_haut_de_gamme.texte: an i9 is a very powerful processor, designed for very heavy workloads
a1.surcharge: Overloaded right now: too many tasks waiting
a2.comp: RAM is your computer's workbench: everything you open is placed there to be used very quickly. When you switch off, the workbench is cleared.
a2.pleine: Memory almost full, to free up
a5.comp: The graphics card is your computer's painter: it draws everything shown on screen (windows, videos, games). It is also what decides how smoothly images move.
a5.no_o: No graphics card could be identified. Why: the detection tool may be missing, or the computer may not have one.
a8.comp: Devices are everything you plug into the computer: keyboard, mouse, USB stick, webcam, printer. Each one needs to be recognised by the system to work.
a8.no_o: No USB device is detected right now. Why: nothing is plugged in, or your keyboard and mouse connect in another way.
a8.liste.texte: This list is enough to check that everything you have plugged in is recognised, so it is ready to use. If a device is missing, try another cable or another port, because the system can only use what it recognises.
b4.comp: This page shows how full each storage space on your computer is, and what it is used for.
b4.critique.titre: A partition is almost full: free up space quickly
b4.critique.texte: Above 90%, the computer slows down and may no longer be able to save files. Free up space now.
b4.surveiller.titre: A partition is filling up: keep an eye on it
b4.surveiller.texte: Above 75%, consider deleting or moving large files (videos, downloads).
b4.ok.texte: No partition is close to full: you can carry on without worry.
b5.nobox.texte: The problem is between your computer and the box: check the cable or the Wi-Fi, then restart the box.
b5.noinet.titre: Local network works, but no internet
b5.noinet.texte: The box responds, so your computer is fine: the problem comes from the box or your provider. Restart the box, and if it persists, contact your provider.
b5.instable.texte: Packets are being lost: this causes cut-offs and slowdowns. Check the cable or move closer to the box.
b5.nodns.titre: Internet responds, but site names are not resolved
b5.nodns.texte: Sites will not open by their name: the directory service (DNS) is down, restart the box.
b5.saine.texte: Every link responds well: browsing, videos and updates work normally.
b5.surveiller.texte: Every link responds, but {dr} packet(s) out of {tot} were lost on the way ({pct} % of the traffic). Why keep an eye on it: lost packets have to be requested again, which slows pages and makes videos stutter.
b5.mauvaise.texte: {dr} packet(s) dropped ({pct} %) and {er} error(s): useful data is being lost.
b5.mauvaise.wifi: Move closer to the box, or use a cable if possible.
b5.mauvaise.cable: Restart the box. If the problem persists, report it to your Internet provider, noting the date and time.
b5.qualite.erreurs_pourquoi: Why: these packets arrived damaged (faulty cable, socket or network card). Zero is the expected result.
b5.qualite.trames: Frames not meant for your computer: {dr} out of {tot} frames, or {pct} % of the traffic
b5.qualite.trames_quoi: What it is: network management messages (CPL adapters, box) that your computer receives without expecting them. It discards them. This is not a loss for you: your pages and videos are not affected.
b5.qualite.reelles: Real losses measured to the box and to the Internet: box {gl} %, Internet {il} %.
b5.comp: This page shows whether your computer's door to the Internet works: the connection, what travels through it, its quality and its speed.
b5.no_o: No active connection is detected. Why: the cable is unplugged, the Wi-Fi is off or the box is switched off. Nothing works without a connection: check the cable and the box.
b5.debit.excellent: excellent: enough for every use, even 4K video and large downloads
b5.debit.correct: fine for the Internet and video, slower for large files
b5.debit.lent: very slow: check the cable, it may be damaged
b5.trafic.dl: You receive far more than you send: this is normal, because browsing, watching a video or updating mostly means downloading.
b5.trafic.up: You send more than you receive: this is unusual. It may come from an online backup or from sending large files.
b5.trafic.equilibre: Receiving and sending are close: balanced use.
b6.comp: This page checks that the small invisible programs that make your computer work are all running properly.
b6.ok.texte: No service reports a problem: the network, the clock, scheduled tasks and the rest are working normally, so there is nothing to do.
b6.un.titre_t: {t} service(s) in error: to check, no rush
b6.un.texte: One or two services in error usually do not block the computer, because each service is independent. Read the cards above and try restarting the listed services.
b6.plusieurs.titre_t: {t} services in error: to deal with
b6.plusieurs.texte: Several services in error at the same time may point to a common problem (network, full disk, interrupted update). Start with the disk (B4) and the network (B5), then restart the listed services.
b6.cause.code: the program stopped with an error (code {ex})
b6.cause.plante: the program was stopped abruptly, it crashed
b6.cause.pas_repondu: the program did not respond in time at startup or shutdown
b6.cause.renonce: the program crashed several times in a row: the system gave up restarting it
b6.cause.dependance: it depends on another service that did not start
b6.cause.ressources: the system did not have enough resources to start it
b6.role.reseau_attente: waits for the network to be ready before the startup goes on. Often harmless if the network arrives late.
b6.role.bluetooth: manages Bluetooth (headphones, mouse, wireless controller). If in error: Bluetooth will not work, the rest still does.
b6.role.cups: manages printing. If in error: printing is impossible.
b6.role.modem: manages 3G/4G sticks and modems. Not applicable if you have none.
b6.role.ssh: lets you connect to this computer remotely. If in error: nobody can connect remotely.
b6.role.web: local web server. If in error: the sites hosted here are unreachable.
b6.role.disques: monitors the health of the disks. If in error: failure alerts will no longer be sent.
b6.role.cron: runs scheduled tasks (backups, cleaning). If in error: they no longer run.
b6.svc.reseau.pourquoi: it connects the computer to the Internet.
b6.svc.heure.pourquoi: it sets the clock from the Internet; a wrong time blocks some sites and updates.
b6.svc.cron.pourquoi: it runs the planned cleaning and backups by itself.
b6.svc.ssh.pourquoi: it lets you connect to the computer from another device; if it is stopped, nobody can connect remotely.
b6.svc.wifi.pourquoi: it connects the computer to wireless networks.
b6.nondispo.bluetooth: this computer has no Bluetooth module, so the service has nothing to manage. Its being stopped is normal and has no consequence.
b6.nondispo.wifi: this computer has no Wi-Fi module, so the service has nothing to manage. Its being stopped is normal and has no consequence.
b6.detail_titre: Details of the services in error
b7.comp: This page shows all the programs running right now, including the ones you cannot see, and which ones weigh the most.
b7.role.systemd: The conductor of the system: it starts and watches all the other services. Without it, nothing starts.
b7.role.systemd_dbus_daemon_dbus_broker: Internal service that lets programs talk to each other and manage the system (log, time, connections).
b7.role.networkmanager_wpa_supplicant: Manages the connection to the network and the Internet.
b7.role.sshd_ssh: Lets you connect to the computer remotely.
b7.role.xorg_xwayland_gnome_shell_plasma: Draws your desktop, the windows and the screen. Without it, you see nothing.
b7.role.gdm_lightdm_sddm: Shows the login screen and opens your session.
b7.role.firefox_chrome_chromium_brave: Your Internet browser: it displays websites.
b7.role.web_content_webextensions_isolat: Parts of the browser: each tab or extension runs in its own process.
b7.role.python_node_java: A program written in a scripting language (or a development tool). Here it can be the DMP server itself.
b7.role.bash_sh_zsh_dash_fish: A terminal (the window where commands are typed) or the script running in it.
b7.role.avahi_daemon: Helps the computer find printers and devices on the local network.
b8.comp: This page measures how long your computer takes to start, from pressing the power button until the desktop is ready, and what slows it down.
b8.no_o: The measurement is not available. Why: the systemd-analyze tool is missing, or the startup has not finished.
b9.comp: This page checks that the doors of your computer are properly closed: security updates, firewall, open doors and recent access.
b9.ok.texte: No update is waiting, no door is open for no reason, nothing to report: the main entrances are closed.
b9.quelques.titre: Protected, a few points to improve
b9.quelques.texte: Nothing serious: the system is not in immediate danger, but some points above (ordinary updates, firewall) are worth fixing when you can.
b9.failles.texte: A serious point is reported (a security update is waiting, too many doors are open, or remote administrator access is enabled).
c1.comp: Updates are vaccines for your computer: each time a flaw or a defect is discovered in a program, the publisher releases a fix. Installing it protects you.
c2.comp: A package is a piece of software stored in the Debian library, ready to be installed or removed cleanly. This page shows which ones are installed, which are the heaviest, and whether anything is broken.
c3.comp: Maintenance means removing what is no longer useful: unused software, copies of downloads, caches. Why: a clean system stays faster and keeps more free space.
c4.comp: Technical information is your computer's identity card: model, system, version. Why: when you ask for help, these details let someone understand exactly your setup.
d1.comp: Searching means finding a topic without going through every page: you type a word in the search box, and DMP shows the pages that talk about it.
d1.x: If no result appears, try a shorter or simpler word ('disk' rather than 'partition'). Each result takes you to the page concerned.
d2.noyau: NO: without a kernel, the computer does not start. Debian keeps the old one as a backup, leave it alone.
d2.firefox: If you uninstall Firefox, you will no longer be able to browse the web with this browser. Keep it if you use it.
d2.grub: NO: GRUB starts Debian when the computer is switched on. Removing it can make the computer impossible to start and prevent future kernel updates.
d2.docker: If you uninstall Docker, the applications running in containers will stop working. Keep it if you do not know what it does.
d2.gnome_aide: If you uninstall this help, you will no longer have the GNOME user guide in the menu. Not serious, but useful when in doubt.
d2.gnome_fonds: If you uninstall these wallpapers, you will no longer be able to choose the desktop images supplied with GNOME. The desktop still works.
d2.libreoffice_writer: If you uninstall LibreOffice Writer, you will no longer be able to open or edit your Word or OpenDocument documents.
d2.libreoffice_aide: If you uninstall the LibreOffice help, you will no longer have the built-in user guide. Your documents stay intact.
d2.locales_all: This package installs all the system languages. You only use one: removing it frees space without breaking anything. Your active language stays in place.
d2.comp: Removing means uninstalling software you no longer need. This page shows you the biggest ones, what they are for and how to remove them safely.
d2.x: DMP removes nothing: this page shows you what, why and how, and you keep the decision. Simple rule for beginners: do not remove anything here if you do not know what a name means.
d3.comp: Benefits are what you gain by looking after your computer well: it stays fast and safe, and it lasts longer.
d3.x: The more ✅ you have, the more you benefit from regular maintenance. A 🟡 is not a failure: it is a gain still possible, explained on the page concerned.
f2_1.comp: Backups are insurance for your files: they are useless until the day you need them, and on that day they save everything. This page checks whether a copy exists and how recent it is.
f2_1.none.titre: No backup of your files: to watch
f2_1.tool.titre: Backup tool installed, no copy found: to watch
f2_1.ancienne.titre: Last backup is old ({date}): to watch
f2_1.ancienne.texte: The last copy dates from {jours} days ago. The older it is, the more work you could lose in case of a failure. Start a Pika backup and schedule it (at least once a week).
f2_1.recente.texte: A Pika Backup copy is {jours} day(s) old: your files are protected. Plug in the backup drive from time to time so DMP can check it.
f3.comp: The speed test (benchmark) is like timing a runner: the computer does an identical effort each time, so the results can be compared over time.
f3.rapide.texte: All three measurements are good: processor, memory and disk keep up. Repeat this test from time to time: a clear drop signals a problem (tired disk, program running in the background).
f3.moyenne.texte: At least one measurement is only fair. Nothing abnormal for everyday use. If the machine seems slow to you, the measurement shows which part is the limit.
f3.faible.texte: At least one measurement is low: that is the part limiting your computer. The disk is the easiest to improve (a SSD is a major gain).
a1.observations: Your processor is a "{m}". It has {c} cores. A core is like a worker: the more there are, the more the work is shared and the faster it gets done. With {c} cores, that is {q}. Current load: {l}. This value measures how many tasks are waiting for their turn: if it stays below {c}, the processor works without being overwhelmed, because each core has its own task. Above {c}, tasks queue up and the computer slows down.
a2.observations: Your computer has {t} GB of memory, {q}. Right now {p} % is in use and {d} GB is free. Why this matters: when the workbench is full, the computer has to store things on the disk, which is much slower, and everything slows down. As long as there is free space, everything stays smooth.
a3.observations:
A disk is the cabinet where your documents, photos, programs and the system are kept for good. Unlike memory, it keeps everything when you switch off.

Why this page: knowing your computer's cabinets, their size and type, is knowing where to store things and what to back up.

🔎 {n} disk(s) detected on this computer:{d}

🏠 Main disk (the one holding the system): size {s}, {p} used ({u} used, {a} free)
   Why: a disk that is too full slows the computer down, prevents updates and saving new files. Below 75 %, you are fine.
a4.observations: Your computer is connected {k}, through the interface "{f}". Its network address is {a}: it is like its house number, which lets other devices find it. Why this matters: without this address, no web page or update could reach you.
a5.observations: Your computer uses: "{g}". {k} Why it is useful to know: it tells you whether the computer can handle games or video editing, or whether it is rather meant for everyday use.
a6.observations: Your motherboard is a "{n}" from the manufacturer {v}. Its startup program (BIOS) is version {b}, dated {y}. Why it is useful: the BIOS is the first program started when you switch on the computer. A very old version may lack fixes, but it is only changed when necessary.
a7.observations: You are using {p}. Its kernel (the heart of the system, which talks directly to the hardware) is version {k}, for the {m} architecture. Why it matters: knowing the version tells you whether it is still supported and updated. Debian is known for its stability.
a9.observations: Your battery is charged to {p} % (status: {s}). Why it is useful: it tells you how long you can work without being plugged in. A battery that no longer lasts as long is worn out over the years.
b1.observations:
⏱️ Up since: {t} (started on {dep})

⚙️ Processor load: {l} for {c} cores
Why: as long as this number stays below {c}, each core has its own task and the computer stays smooth.
b2.observations:
📊 The processor is working at {p} % right now.

The 3 programs using it the most:
{top}

Why: a processor at 100 % for a long time makes the computer slow, because it has no free time left for new requests.
b3.observations:
🧠 Memory used: {p} % of {t} GB (of which {a} GB is still available)

The 3 biggest consumers:
{top}

🔁 Backup memory (swap, on the disk): {sf} GB used out of {st} GB
Why: when the workbench is full, the system stores things on the disk, which is much slower. A lot of swap in use means memory has run short.
b5.trafic:
📦 What has travelled since power-on ({ut})
   • ⬇️ Received: {rh} (about {ph} photos of 1 MB), in {rp} packets
   • ⬆️ Sent: {th}, in {tp} packets
   • Average received: about {mh} per hour
      Why: a packet is a small parcel of data; a web page or a video arrives as thousands of parcels. {bal}
e3_3.observations: History of the last 10 reports available
e4_2.observations: All figures are valid and consistent
e5.observations: System up since: {uptime} | Average load (last minute): {load} (0 to 4 on 4 cores is normal)
f1_3.observations: No anomaly detected. Your system is normal.
f4.observations: Last system change: {last} | Number of changes: {changes} (installations/removals)
verdict.stop: ⛔ Keep: essential to the system. Do not disable or remove.
verdict.judge: 🟠 Do not touch without understanding it: removing this service can break startup, an update or the display. If in doubt, leave it.
verdict.leg: Legend: ⛔ keep · 🟠 do not touch without understanding it
verdict.firmware: The firmware is stored on the motherboard: it cannot be uninstalled and has nothing to do with Debian. Only a BIOS/UEFI setting (fast boot, disk order) can shorten this step.
verdict.vx.rapide: Under 30 seconds is a good result: nothing to improve. The longest step is {n}.
verdict.vx.correct: Between 30 and 60 seconds is acceptable. The longest step is {n}.
verdict.vx.lent: Beyond one minute, something is slowing down startup. The longest step is {n}. Look at the 8 slowest services and check the disk health (Disk page B4): a tired disk is a common cause.
verdict.role.gnome_software: GNOME app store: it installs and updates your software. Closing it does not affect the desktop.
verdict.role.mutter: GNOME window manager: it places and draws the windows on screen. Without it, there is no graphical desktop.
verdict.role.xdg_desktop_portal: bridge between applications and the desktop: it handles opening files and dialog boxes. Useful for recent software.
verdict.role.evolution_alarm: reminders and alarms of the Evolution mail program (calendar). Closing it removes the reminders, without touching the emails.
verdict.role.evolution_source: account and calendar management for Evolution (mail). Closing it deletes nothing, but accounts sync less often.
verdict.role.utility_utility: service process for an application (often the browser or a desktop program). Do not stop it by hand: it restarts with the application.
verdict.role.containerd_containerd_io_ru: container engine (used by Docker and some tools). Removing this service can break Docker or the applications that depend on it.
verdict.role.linux_image: Linux kernel, the core of the system
verdict.role.linux_headers_linux_kbuild_: files needed to compile kernel modules
verdict.role.libllvm: compiler library used by graphics drivers
verdict.role.libc6_libc_bin: standard C library, the base of the system
b5.unstable.texte: Packets are being lost: this causes cut-offs and slowdowns. Check the cable or move closer to the box.
b6.intro: A service is a small invisible program that works in the background, like the staff of a hotel: you do not see it, but the network, printing, the clock or the sound depend on it. Why this page: if an employee falls ill, a function can stop without your understanding why straight away.
